working_application_proof.proof: Keep the ACTUAL marked semistable formal model F_g and invertible M_g of working260, with generic bundle the SAME original M^k. This addendum does not grant or independently settle every construction in260. In particular the horizontal formal-etale Cartier step remains an explicit source/application obligation.

BPR1404.0279v1 whole4.1 defines an admissible R-algebra as an R-flat restricted-power-series quotient by a FINITELY GENERATED ideal. Consequently every actual affine chart of the admissible semistable model gives a finitely presented scheme modulo any nonzero topologically nilpotent a. The finite chart cover of the actual proper model makes X1=F_g modulo a a finite-type scheme over S1=Spec(R/aR), and its residue fibre is the actual proper nodal curve. No Noetherianity of R/aR is inferred.

Here R=C-circle has rank one. For every b in its maximal ideal m, some power b^N has norm at most |a| and belongs to aR; hence radical(aR)=m. Spec(R/aR) has exactly ONE point s, with residue field C-tilde. The ideal m/aR is nil (every element is nilpotent), possibly with NO uniform exponent. The residue base Spec(C-tilde) is a thickening inclusion into S1 in the Stacks sense, and the actual residual curve is exactly the fibre-base-change Xs=X1 times_S1 Spec(C-tilde).

Check properness on the actual whole-mod-a scheme, rather than replacing it with its fibre. Stacks37.3.4(8), Tag0BPG, applies to the morphism of these thickenings because X1->S1 and Xs->Spec(C-tilde) are locally of finite type and the square is the exact base-change square. It transfers properness of the actual residual curve to X1->S1 without a globally nilpotent ideal hypothesis. Its printed proof uses invariance of quasi-compactness, universal closedness and separatedness across thickenings and the locally-finite-type hypothesis. Proper formal-model terminology also encodes this properness; the explicit reduction check avoids relying on terminology alone.

The residue restriction Ms=M_g|Xs has strictly POSITIVE degree on EVERY one-dimensional irreducible component, including every newly introduced bend component, by the actual Cartier degree computation proposed in260. This premise is about the actual original bundle restriction, not a graph measure or an analytic MA coefficient. The field curve is reduced nodal here, but Stacks33.44.15 is more general: on any proper dimension<=1 scheme over a FIELD, an invertible bundle is ample iff each one-dimensional reduced irreducible component has positive degree. It therefore makes Ms ample.

The WHOLE printed proof33.44.15 passes to the finite SURJECTIVE disjoint union of reduced components and isolated closed points. It uses the two-way finite ampleness theorem30.17.2 ONLYover proper FIELD schemes, which are Noetherian, and33.44.14 on each actual integral component. This is a valid use of that Noetherian theorem; it is not its invalid two-way application over C-circle. The complete immediate proof33.44.14 uses the Euler-characteristic growth of positive degree, a nonzero power-section with affine nonvanishing locus, and eventual H1 vanishing via finite-dimensional surjective multiplication maps and the affine-locus cohomology limit.

Apply the GENERAL proper morphism theorem Stacks37.50.3, Tag0D2S, to f:X1->S1, the actual invertible M1=M_g modulo a, and the sole point s. Its hypotheses are proper morphism, invertible sheaf, and ample restriction on the fibre. No Noetherian base, flatness or finite-presentation strengthening is required by the statement. It gives an open neighborhood W of s on which M1 is relatively ample. Because S1 has ONE point, W=S1. Thus M1 is relatively ample on the ENTIRE actual modulo-a scheme. Since S1 is affine, M1 is also ample as an invertible sheaf on X1.

The full printed proof37.50.3 first represents the proper morphism as a limit of proper morphisms over finite-type Z-schemes with affine transitions (32.13.3), descends the invertible sheaf (32.10.3), descends fibre ampleness after enlarging the index (32.4.15), applies Noetherian30.21.4 at that finite stage, and pulls the open neighborhood back. The actual map to the finite-stage base change is affine, so forward pullback of ampleness29.38.7 and base-change29.38.9 apply. Whole30.21.4 was also ROOTread: sufficiently high fibre sections lift by30.21.3, properness removes the common-zero locus near the fibre, and the resulting projective morphism is finite after shrinking by30.21.2; forward finite pullback gives ampleness. These limit/cohomology lemmas are ordinary recursive source dependencies, not independently accepted new grants here.

This settles the immediate positive-component FIELD criterion and exact whole-mod-a relative-ampleness application proposed in260.A12, conditional on the ACTUAL pair and positive Cartier degrees. It avoids every global nilpotence claim and every Noetherian argument directly on R/aR. It does not establish horizontal Cartier closure, full formal H0 GAGA, actual global-section comparison or FS recognition by itself. Working256/259 address separate immediate primary applications; whole250 remains FAILED and must be reconstructed in a new exact scope. Genuine raw coefficients require263 and its canonical-field/chart hypotheses.
